data.keyword: What's the best payment processor for a small online store?

result.keyword: What's the best payment processor for a small online store?
result.markdown:
For a small online store in the UK, I'd put **Stripe and Shopify Payments** at the top of the list.

The best choice depends mainly on what platform your store uses, how much you sell, and whether you want the simplest setup or more flexibility.

My general recommendation\:

- **Stripe** – best all-round payment processor for flexibility and ease of integration.
- **Shopify Payments** – best if your store runs on Shopify.
- **PayPal** – best as an additional payment option to give customers more choice.
- **Square** – worth considering if you sell both online and in person.

## UK fee comparison

These are the published standard rates I found for UK businesses\:

| Provider | Standard online UK card fee |
|--------|--------|
| Stripe | 1.5% + 20p |
| Square | 1.4% + 25p |
| Shopify Payments | 2% + 25p on Basic |
| PayPal | 2.9% + fixed fee |


Sources: official [Stripe pricing](https://stripe.com/gb/pricing), [Square fees](https://squareup.com/gb/en/legal/general/fees), [Shopify pricing](https://www.shopify.com/uk/pricing) and [PayPal fees](https://www.paypal.com/uk/business/paypal-business-fees)\. [stripe.com](https://stripe.com/GB/pricing?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[squareup.com](https://squareup.com/gb/en/legal/general/fees?country_redirection=true&utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.shopify.com](https://www.shopify.com/uk/pricing?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.paypal.com](https://www.paypal.com/uk/business/paypal-business-fees?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

*Rates can vary by card type, customer location and payment method.*

## My recommendations

**1\. Stripe – best overall**

- Straightforward pay-as-you-go pricing.
- No monthly fee on standard pricing.
- Supports Apple Pay, Google Pay and many international payment methods.
- Strong fraud detection and subscription billing options.
- Integrates with many ecommerce platforms.

**2\. Shopify Payments – best for Shopify stores**

- Built directly into Shopify.
- No separate payment gateway to configure.
- No additional Shopify third-party transaction fee when it's your sole payment provider.
- Simple order, refund and payout management. [help.shopify.com](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/payments/shopify-payments/onboarding/cost-of-shopify-payments?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[help.shopify.com](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/payments/shopify-payments/supported-countries/united-kingdom/payment-methods?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**3\. Square – best for online and physical sales**

- No monthly fee on its free plan.
- Useful if you sell at markets, pop-ups or retail premises as well as online.
- Combines online payments and point-of-sale tools. [squareup.com](https://squareup.com/gb/en/legal/general/fees?country_redirection=true&utm_source=chatgpt.com)[squareup.com](https://squareup.com/gb/en/pricing?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**4\. PayPal – best as an additional option**

I'd offer PayPal alongside card payments rather than make it your only processor. It gives customers another familiar way to pay, including those who prefer not to enter card details.

## What I'd choose

For a new, relatively small UK online store\:

- If you're using WooCommerce, Wix or a custom website: **Stripe**\.
- If you're using Shopify: **Shopify Payments**, with PayPal as an additional option.
- If you're selling online and at physical markets: **Square**\.

I'd avoid signing up to a provider with a monthly contract or minimum processing commitment until your sales volume justifies it.

**What platform is your online store built on?**
